changes.locus: Body line 5, x-overtyped tail immediately before partira
changes.evidence: Crop 09 shows two dense x-covered positions between the first word and the space before partira. The underlying word or tail is not securely legible. H passes directly from elle to partira.

Crop 12 shows a compact dense block between the separately visible fasci and le. Its joined upper contour and right upright allow m or crowded/coalesced cu; the ink does not justify H's certain ordinary spelling or a correction chronology.

changes.locus: Body line 8, clipped initial of die
changes.evidence: Crop 13 shows only a tall stem and foot of the first character; its bowl is cut away. The following ie and period are clear. C's unmarked d is too certain; H already identifies d as a clipped-letter supply, so there is no separate lexical disagreement with H.

notes.text: The letter is dated Massy le 23.6.1971 and addresses Verdier. It explicitly refers to a letter du 23 Mai. The date is not changed to match H's editorial comparison with another sheet, which was not inspected.
notes.basis: Observation: date, salutation and body line 1; H editorial note identified as editorial, not source text.

notes.text: The surviving text regrets the lack of ce malheureux exer 4.10.6 and mentions sending le fascicule 1 de SGA 4 to the printer. The verb ending after cela a is cut away and remains unfilled.
notes.basis: Observation: body lines 1–4; no mathematical reconstruction or proof check.

notes.text: The person who typed the text is said to termine mainte[missing], then to leave on holiday; Springer returns the rented machine faute d'autres manuscrits. Publication is consequently postponed sine [uncertain d]ie. The suffix after mainte and any following comma are not visible.
notes.basis: Observation and plain-language description of body lines 4–8; clipped words remain marked in the reading.

notes.text: The initial e of envoyé has visible upper ink. The retained source candidates are ènvoyé and ênvoyé; ordinary unaccented envoyé is removed from C's candidate set.

Before partira, the first word's last slot has e and l components with uncertain order, followed by two x-covered positions. The first l is also heavy, but heaviness alone does not support a separate earlier character.
notes.basis: Observation: crop 09; order is explicitly not inferred.

notes.text: The final fascimle/fascicule remains uncertain: a compact block permits m or coalesced cu. The earlier clear fascicule does not decide this later word.
notes.basis: Observation: crop 12; avoidance of contextual spelling repair.

notes.text: The photocopy is clipped on both text edges. The closing is Bien cordialement, without a visible signature; its upper marks belong to ordinary typewritten ascenders and i dots. The otherwise blank lower area carries archive number 12 at lower left.
notes.basis: Observation: whole, both halves, and crop 14; archive number represented only by a TeX comment.

notes.text: No mathematical checking occurred. Exercise and volume numbers were transcribed as references; check_events is empty. Matching H supplied-letter hypotheses at clipped initials are not counted as independent lexical differences merely because their macro syntax differs from unsure; full-word restorations and the added comma are separately collated.
notes.basis: Scope of this independent reader run; comparison method, not a proof event.
